text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The government is to step up a fight against corruption through stricter punishment and the possible establishment of an anti-graft committee.
-- Consumption of liquefied petroleum gas in Vietnam is expected to hit 60,000 tonnes this year from 25,000 in 1995.
-- The National Assembly has nominated Ha Manh Tri as head of the People's Supreme Inspectorate, effectively Vietnam's chief prosecutor.
-- The government has issued new regulations on foreign press activities in Vienam.
-- Some 53 people have been killed by flooding in the central provinces of Quang Nam-Da Nang, Quang Ngai and Kon Tum.
-- Natural disasters have caused damage worth 4,000 billion dong ($363.6 million) so far this year.
-- Vietnam imported 280,000 motorbikes in the first nine months of this year, equivalent to 56.5 percent of the target for the whole year.
